name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
description: A large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. The dataset consists of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages (German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish).
creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert (Facebook AI Research)
inLanguage: en, de, nl, es, fr, pt, it, pl
citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. arXiv:2012.03411v2 [eess.AS], December 22, 2020.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. Audio files were downloaded using LibriLight open source library tools and downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Languages were selected based on the number of audiobook hours and availability of corresponding text sources. Text sources were downloaded from multiple domains including gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, and hathitrust.org for English, with manual approaches incorporated for other languages due to domain diversity and invalid links.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Audio data from LibriVox audiobooks (public domain read speech) and corresponding text from Project Gutenberg and other public domain sources. For acoustic model training used in segmentation and pseudo-labeling, in-house datasets consisting of audio from videos publicly shared by users were used (completely de-identified).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Numbers in the text were replaced with corresponding aligned words from pseudo labels to handle variations in number pronunciation. Heuristics were applied to deal with hyphens and apostrophes, including removing end-of-line hyphenation, replacing rare words with hyphens, and handling double apostrophes.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models with Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions and Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss. Segmentation was performed by running inference to generate viterbi token sequences with timestamps, then splitting at silence intervals. Text normalization included NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters (punctuations, subscript/superscripts, emojis, escape symbols), removal of end-of-line hyphens, and filtering characters outside valid unicode ranges based on language orthography. Books with corrupted metadata, multiple speakers, or dramatic readings were removed. Only the latest version of books sharing the same authors and title were kept. Candidate transcripts with WER >40% between pseudo label and matched text were filtered out.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human evaluation was performed on development and test sets. Human transcribers listened to audio files while viewing transcripts and were asked to correct only 'clear and obvious' errors to ensure high quality without introducing bias. Corrections included diacritic corrections, missing words, and missing apostrophes.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: WER between generated transcripts and human-rated transcripts was measured to assess annotation quality. WER ranged from 1.93% (Spanish dev) to 12.64% (Portuguese dev) across languages.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Trained acoustic models using Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions with Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss were used to generate pseudo labels. For English, a pre-trained model using TDS encoder and CTC loss on LibriSpeech was used. Beam-search decoding with 4-gram language models was performed for pseudo label generation. Smith-Waterman alignment algorithm was used for transcript retrieval. A gender classifier (SVM with RBF kernel trained on LibriSpeech, consuming 40-dimensional log-filterbank features) was used to label speaker gender with 95% test accuracy on LibriSpeech and 94-96% on Dutch and Polish.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender (used for balancing development and test sets)
rai:dataLimitations: For Polish, the out-of-vocabulary (OOV) rate is 13.39%, which negatively impacts WER when performing language model decoding with constrained lexicon. The dataset is read speech, which may limit generalization to conversational or spontaneous speech. English development and test sets were chosen to be harder than LibriSpeech dev-/test-other partitions (speakers with WER higher than 80% of dev-other sets). Text sources for some audiobooks could not be downloaded due to invalid links or domain diversity, resulting in lower training data than the total available LibriVox hours.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is suitable for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) research and Text-To-Speech (TTS) research. It can be used for training, validation, and testing of ASR systems. Limited supervision datasets (10 hour, 1 hour, and six 10-minute sets) are provided for low-resource training benchmarks. The dataset can extend LibriTTS for creating a larger and multilingual version for TTS research. Training and test sets are interchangeable and complementary with LibriSpeech for English.
